title: Des Noyers 1659: Pierre Des Noyers to Ismaël Boulliau, note in cipher on the Spanish marriage and Marie Mancini, [Danzig, December 1659] (BnF Fr. 13020 f. 297): contemporary gloss transcribed, nomenclator rebuilt from the glossed passages of the volume

steps.what: The 1656 sign key (f. 315) tested on the glossed passages: 0/41 agreements on groups 3-39 (controls mean 0.001); no sign of its alphabet.
Table rebuilt from cipher / gloss pairs of 12 passages: 88 groups, 88.8% consistency (code words 97.2%, controls <= 34%).
Leave-one-out check of f. 297 against the other 11 passages: 24 groups, 18 certain, 2 probable, 4 restored from the gloss only.

Write-up session: transcription of f. 297 compared with the full-resolution image (BnF openapi IIIF, view 608): all 24 cipher groups and the gloss words read as transcribed; the small ring written after 10, 21 and 20 could be a mark or a raised zero, and the final word of the note ends in a flourish (dittes / ditte).

Full text of the 1859 edition (Lettres de Pierre Des Noyers, Internet Archive OCR) searched for the note: no "petit billet" of December 1659, no Mancini passage; the letters of 13, 20 and 27 Dec 1659 are printed without it. The other glossed passages are printed in clear there (not re-collated here).

reading.md rewritten as the sentence the note makes: the earlier file put Des Noyers's own plain text in angle brackets, which the readability check counts as gaps (50% clean sentences); as a sentence it scores 1.0. The 88.8% consistency and the 97.2% code-word figure are the contributor's and were not recomputed, since the other glossed passages are not in the repository.

validation.notes: too short: the note has 24 cipher groups (12 words), under the 40-token floor; the key was rebuilt from other passages and checked group by group against the gloss

outcome.method_basis: The note is read from the contemporary interlinear gloss on the manuscript, which deciphered it at the time and is not a new decipherment; the 00-99 nomenclator in key.tsv is a key rebuilt here from adjacent glossed plaintext, the eleven other glossed passages of the same volume (Fr. 13020, 1658-1659), and is not the 1656 sign key of f. 315.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 12/12 cipher words of the note have a value from the contemporary gloss (6 certain and 2 probable against the table rebuilt from the other passages, 4 restored from the gloss alone); the rebuilt table independently supports 8 of 12.

credits.note: the interlinear gloss of the time on f. 297 (probably Boulliau's hand) gives the clear text of every cipher group; the eleven other glossed passages of Fr. 13020 (1658-1659) give the values the key was rebuilt from

PR #263: cipher and gloss of f. 297 transcribed and checked group by group; the 00-99 nomenclator with marks rebuilt from the glossed passages of Fr. 13020 (key.tsv); the 1656 key of f. 315 ruled out; English translation. Content existing (contemporary gloss), not a solution

texts.label: Pierre Des Noyers to Ismaël Boulliau, note in cipher, [Dec 1659]
texts.summary: Des Noyers tells Boulliau he has seen his little note and is sure that, but for the Queen, nobody would wait for the death of the Prince of Spain to break off the marriage, and that la Mancini must be very bold to try what Boulliau reports of her. The five ciphered phrases are the sense of the note; the rest is plain text.
texts.note: Existing: the text is the contemporary interlinear gloss, checked group by group against the table rebuilt from the other passages; 12 cipher words, 6 certain, 2 probable, 4 restored from the gloss alone, 0 unresolved. Which Queen and which Mancini the note means is not stated on it: Anne of Austria and Marie Mancini are the contributor's reading from the context.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (Claude Sonnet 5.5, write-up session for Daniel Bourdeau; a model reading against the image, not a person)
reading_review.note: Read as a sentence against the full-resolution image: one complete French sentence of 1659 (despagne, ardie = hardie, dittes), 40 words of which 12 come from the cipher, with no hole; the cipher words agree with the gloss written above them. The earlier 50% sentence score came from the markup of reading.md, not from the text. The sentence is short and its political sense (which Queen, which Mancini) is an interpretation; no person has read it.

prior.where: Contemporary interlinear gloss on the manuscript itself (BnF Fr. 13020 f. 297): a hand of the time, probably Boulliau's (the attribution is the contributor's, not checked against his hand), wrote the clear word above every cipher group. Not in the 1859 edition of the letters (Internet Archive OCR searched here), which prints the other glossed passages of 1658-1659 in clear.

human: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
